chunks: From him, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar ibn Wahb, from Dāwūd ibn Mahziyār, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: A man saw in his sleep and experienced pleasure and desire, then he rose and did not see anything on his garment. He said: So he replied, “If he is ill, then ghusl is upon him; and if he is healthy, then there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.اللَّذَّةَ: physical pleasure experienced in the dream
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath required in certain states of janābah
key_terms.ثَوْبِهِ: his garment, checked for physical trace
key_terms.صَحِيحًا: healthy, for whom no obligation is stated here
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: ill or sick, affecting the legal ruling here

ai.seo_question: Does a person have to perform ghusl after feeling desire in a dream if no trace is found?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who experiences sexual pleasure in sleep but finds no trace on his garment upon waking. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام distinguishes between the sick and the healthy person, ruling ghusl for the former and no obligation for the latter.
